start_here: Say to your AI: "Bring my Claude.ai chat export from Downloads/claude-data into my records, one row per conversation and every message." It runs the import for the claude-ai-export source and tells you how many conversations and messages were kept.

lists.label: AI conversations
lists.holds: One row per conversation you had with an AI: its title, the app, when it started and ended, how many messages and which models; your own labels, people, pursuits and follow-ups are never overwritten by an import.
alike: a notes app folder of saved chats
a research log of AI conversations

instructions: 1. Save your chat app's export in a folder you grant the door (for example Downloads/claude-data/conversations.json), and keep list:ai-conversations (or pour the two example rows into your own chat list, see pour).

2. Ask tool:list-the-conversation-sources-on-this-computer which source id fits the export, then run tool:import-my-conversations-from-a-source with that source (claude-ai-export here); add time_box_seconds for a very large export.

3. Read the answer: conversations_kept and messages_added say what is new; more: true means it stopped at its time box or a busy door, so run it again and it continues from its cursor rows; running it again over a finished file adds nothing.
4. Open list:ai-conversations: each conversation has a row; your labels, people, pursuits and follow-ups stay when you import again.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for your AI chats and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (same id, same label or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than 80% match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the two example rows to your list.
